headline: Protein language models extend to PPIs, PTMs, LLPS, and nucleic acid structure
label: Protein Language Model Applications
summary: Sequence-only deep learning now spans PPI interfaces, PTM syntax, phase separation, and nucleic acid structure in recent work.
synthesis: The common thread is sequence-only prediction built on learned representations, with protein language models supplying features for tasks that previously relied on structure or curated annotation. An ensemble framework using PLM embeddings separates self-separating from partner-dependent phase-separating proteins and scores disease variants in intrinsically disordered regions. ProtSyntax applies a PTM-aware PLM with geometry-constrained attention to 40 PTM-site benchmarks and models PTM crosstalk. X-PAIR and MSA Pairformer extend this to protein-protein interactions: X-PAIR jointly predicts PPIs and partner-specific interfaces with cross-attention, while MSA Pairformer, a 111M-parameter model, applies AlphaFold-style pairwise refinement to interaction coevolution. NUMonomer applies end-to-end deep learning to predict RNA and single-stranded DNA 3D structures from sequence alone. A layer-wise analysis of eight ESM2 and AMPLIFY models locates where proteome-level concept knowledge emerges. The microbial phenotype benchmark of up to 57 general LLMs is a distinct study, where self-reported confidence tracks accuracy.
